stories.title: Never stop questioning, Shivakumar tells young lawyers
stories.summary: Addressing the 34th annual convocation of NLSIU, where the Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, Supreme Court judges, Chief Justice of the Karnataka High Court Vibhu Bakhru and other judges were present, Shivakumar said a strong democracy always allows its people to question.

article_sentences: Addressing the 34th annual convocation of NLSIU, where the Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, Supreme Court judges, Chief Justice of the Karnataka High Court Vibhu Bakhru and other judges were present, Shivakumar said a strong democracy always allows its people to question.

Bengaluru: Chief Minister D K Shivakumar on Saturday asked graduating students of National Law School of India University (NLSIU) to protect democracy, constitutional values and not to stop questioning.
“Never stop questioning, never compromise your values and never forget the people,” Shivakumar told young graduates.
He urged them to defend democratic institutions, uphold constitutional values and make justice accessible to every citizen.

Emphasising that a strong democracy must allow citizens to question the government, Shivakumar said young lawyers and policymakers had a special responsibility to safeguard the Constitution, “particularly at a time when democratic institutions across the world were facing challenges”.
“A strong democracy is not one where everyone agrees with the government.
A strong democracy is one where every citizen has the freedom to question the government,” he said.
The chief minister called on graduates to question, debate and challenge ideas while also taking responsibility for finding solutions.
He said constitutional principles must guide governance, policymaking and public life rather than remain confined to textbooks.
“India does not simply need more lawyers.
We need lawyers with integrity, compassion and courage,” he said, urging young lawyers to understand the struggles of ordinary people and stand up for what is right, even when it is difficult.

Shivakumar also announced that the Karnataka government will establish a dedicated institute to train law graduates for judicial service examinations and provide continuing education for young lawyers.

stories.headline: Cabinet approves new industrial policy with focus on non-polluting sectors
stories.title: Cabinet approves new industrial policy with focus on non-polluting sectors
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'cabinet approves' in title weight 44
candidate gate: no category but HIGH+ priority -> allowed
article_sentences: The Delhi government has approved a new industrial policy that outlines a ten-year roadmap for developing a clean, knowledge-based industrial economy in the Capital, with a focus on high-value, non-polluting sectors, according to a statement from the Chief Minister’s Office (CMO) said on Wednesday.

The Industrial Policy, 2026, approved in a Cabinet meeting chaired by Chief Minister Rekha Gupta, also allocated Rs 1,000 crore under Mukhyamantri Udyamshree Yojana for five years to promote new industries and create jobs, said the statement.

Under the new policy, special incentives will be given for 10 priority sectors, including Information Technology (IT), global capability centres, data centres, healthcare, research and modern manufacturing, as per the CMO.
“Women-led micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) will receive additional support for business modernisation and expansion.
Employers hiring women will receive higher incentives for each woman recruited.
Women and young people will also receive special attention under skill development programmes.
These provisions aim to expand business and employment opportunities for women entrepreneurs and employees,” said the statement.
Ms. Gupta said the policy focuses on making better use of the Capital’s economic potential by encouraging advanced technology, research, specialised services and high-value-added industries.

“Over the next 10 years, it aims to create an investment-friendly environment, provide necessary support to entrepreneurs, promote women-led enterprises and generate new employment opportunities for young people.
It will also seek to steer Delhi’s industrial economy towards a more modern, cleaner and knowledge-based model,” she said.

Ms. Gupta said that considering the needs of different sectors, tailored incentives would be provided for capital investment, office or workspace rentals, new hiring, research, certification, technological modernisation, energy conservation and skill development.
The policy will also encourage resource reuse and waste reduction, she added.

stories.headline: Delhi protests: Metro was ‘fully functional’, 32 lakh rode trains on October 10: DMRC tells Supreme Court
stories.title: Delhi protests: Metro was ‘fully functional’, 32 lakh rode trains on October 10: DMRC tells Supreme Court
stories.summary: Admits commuter traffic ‘slightly lower’ than usual second-Saturday count of 58 lakh, says protests may have dampened people’s willingness to travel
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) and its chairperson filed separate affidavits in the Supreme Court on Wednesday (October 14, 2026), stating that the Metro network remained “fully functional” on October 10, recording 32 lakh passengers.
“There was zero reduction in the total volume of metro operation or the number of train trips,” the DMRC said.

Though the DMRC admitted that commuter traffic was “slightly lower” than the typical 58 lakh passengers on a “normal” second Saturday, it attributed the drop to public caution amid protests rather than administrative paralysis.
It said ordinary citizens were “compelled to forgo their usual day-to-day activities” on October 10.
The day saw heavy security crackdowns in the capital against demonstrations demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

Petitioners like CPI(M) general secretary M.A. Baby and advocate Shailendra Mani Tripathi had argued that widespread barricading and station closures violated an October 9 Supreme Court order mandating proportionate movement restrictions.
Defending its actions, the DMRC said entry and exit regulations were limited to 45 of the network’s 303 stations on October 10.
Though the initial count of the number of stations to be closed on October 10 was 57, it was scaled down to 45, accounting for about 15% of the network.
“Over 85% of the network (258 stations) remained fully operational, accessible, and functional for commuters,” the DMRC stated.

Crucially, of the 45 stations where entry and exit gates were regulated, 14 key interchange stations (including major transit hubs such as Rajiv Chowk, Kashmere Gate, Central Secretariat, Mandi House, Hauz Khas, Dilli Haat-INA, and Netaji Subhash Place) continued to provide full and uninterrupted line-interchange facilities for commuters.
Commuters entering the city as well as inside the city were able to change transit corridors seamlessly without disruption, the affidavit said.
“For the limited stations where passenger gates were regulated, other Metro stations had remained open to minimise inconvenience to the travelling public,” the affidavit noted.

stories.headline: Supreme Court asks Delhi governmente to seek inputs from IB on Hawara plea for transfer to Punjab jail
stories.title: Supreme Court asks Delhi governmente to seek inputs from IB on Hawara plea for transfer to Punjab jail
stories.summary: Bench takes a cautious approach, saying the case of Beant Singh murder convict is sensitive, and even the Punjab government seems to be reluctant
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Tuesday (October 13, 2026) asked the Delhi government to seek inputs from the Intelligence Bureau (IB) on Beant Singh murder convict Jagtar Singh Hawara’s plea for transfer from Delhi’s Tihar jail to a prison in Punjab.
A Bench headed by Justices M.M. Sundresh and P.B. Varale took a cautious approach, saying the case was sensitive, and even the Punjab government seemed to be reluctant.
“We know that every sinner has a future… Like how somebody said, if you kill a single person, you are a murderer.
Kill a few thousand, you are a conqueror… But we will have to look at the implications of the transfer on the society,” Justice Sundresh said.

Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati, appearing for the Delhi government, informed the top court that Hawara was involved in a jailbreak and his death penalty was converted to life imprisonment in the murder case.
Contending that transfer might increase chances of his escape, Ms. Bhati referred to an advisory by the Ministry of Home Affairs on transfer of high-risk prisoners.
Senior advocate Colin Gonsalves, for Hawara, said he had personally visited his client in jail and found him completely reformed.
Ms. Bhati referred to a Punjab government affidavit which sounded apprehensive about the effect of Hawara’s shift on the law and order situation in the State.
Mr. Gonsalves submitted that the assassination of the Chief Minister happened in 1995 when his client was only 21 years old.
“His mother is very old, 82 years old and in serious condition.
He is only seeking a transfer to a Punjab high-security prison, and not seeking release.
He has a blemishless record in jail,” Mr. Gonsalves argued.

stories.title: Supreme Court probe panel to prioritise use of pellet gun, harassment of female protesters during July 20 march to Parliament
stories.summary: A statement by the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) said that for the convenience of the affected people, including the affected police personnel, the high-powered enquiry committee (HPEC) has launched a portal — http://hpec.nic.in

event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court-appointed panel to investigate the incidents of violence at Jantar Mantar in Delhi and places outside the national capital in July during the NEET paper leak protests will prioritise matters related to the “use of pellet guns, targeted violence and harassment of female protesters, and excessive violence and destruction of property occasioned on either side”.

A statement by the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) on behalf of the Supreme Court-constituted High Powered Enquiry Committee (HPEC) said that for the convenience of the affected people, including the affected police personnel, the HPEC has launched a portal — http://hpec.nic.in.
“The HPEC shall examine all issues enumerated in paragraphs 12 and 13 of the Hon’ble Supreme Court’s order dated 18 August 2026 and paragraph 5(i) of order dated 10 September, 2026.

Priority will be given to matters pertaining to the use of pellet guns, targeted violence and harassment of female protestors, and excessive violence and destruction of property occasioned on either side,” the statement said.

The Hindu was the first to report on July 21 that at least one protester was hit by a pellet gun, part of the anti-riot gear of the Rapid Action Force (RAF) during the July 20 march to Parliament called by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), which turned violent.
Later, three more victims said they had been hit by pellets, usually fired from pump action guns.
Subsequently, on July 28, The Hindu reported that though Delhi.

Police denied the use of pellet guns, a general diary entry filed at Parliament Street police station revealed that the RAF fired two rounds from an anti-riot gun on the directions of a Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP)-rank officer of the police.

The demands for answers by the Opposition parties as to who ordered the use of pellet guns during the protests, in which at least 80 protesters were injured, and women were allegedly sexually assaulted by police personnel, led to the disruption of the monsoon session of Parliament.
The portal is designed in such a manner as to enable due protection to vulnerable witnesses and also to keep the identities confidential and undisclosed, if so wished by the affected persons.
The affected persons and other stakeholders are encouraged to access the portal and upload their complaints/representations making use of the formats as applicable, it said.

“Apart from the above, any person wishing to provide information/suggestion relating to the issues referred to the HPEC under the orders dated 18 August 2026 and 10 September 2026 may also do so through the aforesaid portal.

stories.headline: IMD to expand radar network, strengthen existing ones
stories.title: IMD to expand radar network, strengthen existing ones
stories.summary: Chennai radar was indigenously renovated in 2022, and its functioning is being closely monitored as it would help in cyclone detection
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) is looking to strengthen its existing radar network alongside installing new radars to improve weather observations and track monsoons.
With the onset of Northeast monsoon on Thursday, the IMD’s Regional Meteorological Centre is maintaining the nearly 24-year-old Chennai’s-band doppler weather radar in working condition.
It is likely to be replaced with a new S-band radar by 2027.
Installed as India’s first doppler weather radar in 2002, Chennai’s radar on Rajaji Salai continues to monitor weather up to 400 km.
Officials of the RMC said orders have been placed to replace various radars, including Chennai, Karaikal, Kolkata and Machilipatnam about six months ago.
The supplier is awaiting a component from abroad before assembling the new equipment.
In 2022, Chennai radar was indigenously renovated and its functioning is being closely monitored as it would help in cyclone detection.
Four new S-Band and X-band radars would be installed at Kanniyakumari, Tiruchi, Yercaud and Ramanathapuram under the Mission Mausam.
Radars are being installed across the country in coordination with the respective State governments.
X band radars, which have a weather surveillance range of up to 180 km, would provide accurate observations of extreme weather events, said Sivananda Damodara Pai, Head, RMC.

Mrutyunjay Mohapatra, IMD Director General, said besides the existing weather radars in places like Sriharikota, Pallikaranai, Karaikal and Chennai Rajaji Salai, new radars would cover more areas for weather observations.
Radars being maintained in the neighbouring States also help in Tamil Nadu’s weather surveillance.
